# 1 Chronicles Chapter 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 380v

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** After this, Nahash the king of the Ammonites died, and his son reigned in his place.

**2** David said, "I will deal loyally with Hanun the son of Nahash, for his father dealt loyally with me." So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. When David's servants came to the land of the Ammonites, to Hanun, to comfort him,

**3** the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, "Do you think David is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Have not his servants come to search out, overthrow, and spy on the land?"

**4** So Hanun seized David's servants, shaved them, and cut off their garments at the waist, and sent them away.

**5** When David was told about the men, he sent to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, "Remain at Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return."

**6** When the Ammonites realized they had made themselves repulsive to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.

**7** They hired thirty-two thousand chariots and the king of Maacah with his forces, who came and camped before Medeba. The Ammonites also mustered from their cities and came out for battle.

**8** When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of the mighty men.

**9** The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance of the city, while the kings who had come were by themselves in the open field.

**10** When Joab saw that the battle was set against him both in front and in the rear, he chose the best men in Israel and drew them up against the Arameans.

**11** The rest of the troops he placed under the command of Abishai his brother, and they drew up against the Ammonites.

**12** He said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall come to my aid; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your aid.

**13** Be strong, and let us be courageous for our people and for the cities of our God, and may the LORD do what is good in his sight."

**14** Joab and the troops with him advanced against the Arameans for battle, and they fled before him.

**15** When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother and entered the city. Then Joab returned to Jerusalem.

**16** When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans from beyond the River, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army leading them.

**17** When it was reported to David, he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan. He came upon them and drew up against them. David set the battle in order against the Arameans, and they fought with him.

**18** The Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers, and he killed Shophach the commander of the army.

**19** When Hadadezer's vassals saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. And the Arameans were no longer willing to help the Ammonites.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter parallels 2 Samuel 10 closely. It narrates the transition from attempted diplomacy to full-scale war, triggered by the Ammonites' humiliation of David's envoys. The Chronicler preserves the structure and most details from Samuel, including Joab's remarkable battlefield speech (v.13). The chapter serves as the military prelude to what in Samuel leads to the Bathsheba narrative (2 Sam 11) — but the Chronicler will skip that story entirely in chapter 20, jumping straight to the siege of Rabbah. The numbers in this chapter are characteristically larger than Samuel's parallels (32,000 chariots vs. smaller figures; 7,000 chariots vs. 700 in the final battle).

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.4 — "shaved them" — what was shaved?
- **EMET:** "and-shaved-them [vayegallechem]"
- **LOGOS:** "shaved them"
- **PNEUMA:** "shaved off their beards"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "shaved them" — the Hebrew does not specify "beards" (the parallel in 2 Sam 10:4 says "half their beards"). The Chronicler's briefer version simply says "shaved them." PNEUMA's addition, while historically reasonable, goes beyond this text.

### V.6 — "made themselves odious/repulsive" rendering
- **EMET:** "made-themselves-odious [hit'ba'ashu]"
- **LOGOS:** "made themselves repulsive"
- **PNEUMA:** "made themselves an enemy"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "made themselves repulsive" — the hitpael of *ba'ash* literally means "to make oneself stink." LOGOS preserves the intensity. PNEUMA's "enemy" is too interpretive.

### V.13 — "let us be courageous" vs. "let us show ourselves courageous" vs. "let's fight with everything we have"
- **EMET:** "and-let-us-be-strong [venitkchazaq]"
- **LOGOS:** "let us show ourselves courageous"
- **PNEUMA:** "let's fight with everything we have"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "let us be courageous" — a middle path between EMET's literalism and PNEUMA's expansive paraphrase.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
